name: thReat World Championship
epitaph: thReat's top championship, held across both of its runs. Xaxon won it at ReLoad 2002 from Disciple X and held it until the company closed on 23 June 2002, when the belt was retired. When thReat reopened, General David Sanders beat Xaxon for it at Payback 2003, and was still champion when the title history ends.

events.note: "Belt was retired, due to closure of company on 06/23/02" — the title history's own line; the belt returned with the company in 2003.

name: thReat Tag Team Championship
epitaph: thReat's tag team title, first recorded at Payback 2003, where the brothers of Born To Die beat three other teams for it; they were still champions when the title history ends.

name: thReat International Championship
epitaph: A championship thReat ran in both of its runs. Takisuma Ogama won it from Noah Krone at ReLoad 2002 and held it until the belt was retired with the company's closure on 23 June 2002. Chris McCluskey beat blind for it at Double Or Nothing 2003 and was still champion when the title history ends.

events.note: "Belt was retired, due to closure of company on 06/23/02" — the title history's own line; the belt returned with the company in 2003.

name: thReat Aggression Championship
epitaph: The most travelled of thReat's belts. Riot won it from Lennox Dawson on Sunday Night Flaw 04 and handed it to Lawrence Clementia six weeks later; Rejection beat Clementia for it and held it to the company's closure on 23 June 2002, when the belt was retired. In the 2003 run Steve Solex won it at Malevolence, Wolf took it from him at Payback, and Ernie French took it from Wolf at Double Or Nothing and was still champion when the title history ends.

events.note: "Belt was retired, due to closure of company on 06/23/02" — the title history's own line; the belt returned with the company in 2003.

name: thReat Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: A title of thReat's 2003 run. Vertigo won it from Phil Atken on Sunday Night Flaw 16; Phil Atken took it back at Malevolence 2003 over Vertigo and Tyler Davidson, and Tyler Davidson won it from Atken at Payback 2003 and was still champion when the title history ends.

name: thReat Fighting Championship
epitaph: A championship thReat ran in both of its runs. Quincy Brown won it from Amp Canon at ReLoad 2002 and held it until the belt was retired with the company's closure on 23 June 2002. Vincent Pembridge won it from Jason Semps in a cage on Sunday Night Flaw 18 in 2003 (the fed's title history dates the win to Flaw 17 and counts ninety days), Jere Casarella took it from him on Sunday Night Flaw 25, and psycho-Rio won it from Casarella in a Fight To The Death at Double Or Nothing 2003, still champion when the title history ends.

events.note: "Belt was retired, due to closure of company on 06/23/02" — the title history's own line; the belt returned with the company in 2003.
